objective: Select the next workstream after closing the tracked filelist registry public-pack boundary.

decision.reason: The tracked filelist registry boundary is now public-pack closed, but the staged set is above the documented 100-file commit guard. Before adding native parser, arbitrary filelist planning, dependency inference, allocation broadening, resident optimization, or GEM comparison work, split and clean the public-pack change set so review and hooks remain tractable.

candidate_review.reason: The current staged set is larger than the documented hook limit, so cleanup and split planning is the smallest useful next gate before adding more technical surface.
A parser boundary would add new user-facing implementation scope before the existing public-pack chain is review-sized.
This remains the most direct technical follow-up for filelist-to-GPU automation, but it should start after the current staged chain is split and committed cleanly.
Dependency inference is a broader input-closure problem and should not be mixed into the current tracked-template registry publication.
Automatic allocation broadening needs additional evidence and should not be stacked on top of the current large staged set.
Resident optimization targets repeated-launch weakness and is not the immediate blocker for publishing the current Verilator-like filelist registry chain.
GEM comparison should wait until the reviewed public-pack boundary and commit history are small enough to compare and explain cleanly.

required_next_gate.name: define_commit_split_and_public_pack_cleanup_gate
must_pin: the staged file count before split
the documented commit guard limit for staged non-submodule file changes
which files belong to the Verilator native option filelist registry and public-pack chain
which unrelated or pre-existing staged changes must stay separate
which generated reports or artifacts remain non-canonical
the intended commit groups and the verification commands to rerun after each split
that no new measurement, execution, runtime/ABI, parser, planner, dependency inference, allocation, or GEM claim is introduced

non_claims: not a runtime or ABI change
not a native Verilator parser change
not arbitrary filelist or RTL support
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
